text: We tested label smoothing (coefficient 0.1) applied to the weak supervision targets in a weak-to-strong generalization setup, with qwen2.5-0.5b as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-3b as the strong student, across 3 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.61 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.81. Under label smoothing, the strong student trained on weak labels achieved a transfer accuracy of 0.62 (SE 0.01), corresponding to a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.04 with a standard error of 0.07. The baseline PGR without label smoothing was 0.18. The measured PGR is therefore below the baseline, and with a standard error of 0.07 across only 3 seeds the estimate is too imprecise to support any directional conclusion about the method's effect. We do not observe evidence that label smoothing on weak targets improves weak-to-strong transfer here; further seeds would be needed to characterize the effect with any confidence.
